Without a value the request goes out with the literal placeholder, which the
container rejects with 400 before routing -- so every check on that endpoint
judges a malformed request rather than the API, and the engine now skips them
instead. One value here unlocks roughly twenty assertions per endpoint.
EVERY VALUE MUST NAME A RECORD THAT DOES NOT EXIST.
The same request helper issues DELETEs against UAT on every run. An id that
happens to exist would destroy real data, and the checks that need these are
auth and error-shape checks -- they are satisfied by any well-formed id,
because authentication is evaluated before the id is ever looked up.
Verified against UAT: /delete/1 and /delete/abc both return 401 unauthenticated.
